memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you are harvesting in your field and you overlook a sheaf, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands. - Deut 24:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives a gracious command about harvesting. If a sheaf of grain was accidentally left behind in the field, the farmer was not to go back for it. Instead, it was to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow to gather. God built provision for the poor right into the everyday work of the harvest. The overlooked sheaf became a gift of dignity, allowing the needy to gather food through their own effort.

What a beautiful design. The poor were not simply given handouts, but were allowed to gather for themselves, preserving their dignity. And the well-off were called to hold their possessions with an open hand, not grasping for every last bit, but deliberately leaving margin for others to be blessed. Generosity was woven into the rhythm of ordinary life.

We should be careful with the mention of blessing here. This is not a prosperity formula guaranteeing wealth to the generous. Rather, it reflects God's design that open-handed, generous living aligns us with His heart and His favour. The enduring principle is clear, God calls His people to leave margin in their lives for the sake of others, to not consume everything for themselves but to make room for the needy. Boaz later embodied this beautifully when Ruth gleaned on this very provision (Ruth 2). How might God be inviting you to leave some "sheaves" for others rather than grasping for everything yourself?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you leave margin in your life for the sake of others?
2. Where are you tempted to grasp for every last bit?
3. How can you preserve the dignity of those you help?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me hold my possessions with an open hand, leaving room to bless others. Teach me generosity that honours the dignity of the needy. Amen.
